about: The ambient field's sourced values, as materials.json is for rock: every level carries its source and the line it comes from, or is marked measured by this lab (with its run) or derived. Velocities are RMS, m/s.

sources.peterson1993: Peterson, J.R., 1993, Observations and modeling of seismic background noise: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 93-322, 94 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/ofr93322
sources.m1_01: This lab, run m1_01_ambient_levels: MedNet KEG, Kottamya (29.9275 N, 31.8292 E), twelve days of 1996, open data at INGV, McNamara & Buland (2004) spectra via ObsPy PPSD
sources.elgabry2026: ELGabry, M., Hamed, A., Yoshimura, S., Hussein, H.M., Maklad, M., Salama, A., 2026, Architectural and geotechnical aspects affecting earthquake resilience for the antique Egyptian Khufu pyramid: Scientific Reports 16, 14032, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-49962-6
sources.fta1995: Federal Transit Administration, 1995, Transit Noise and Vibration Impact Assessment, Chapter 7, Basic Ground-Borne Vibration Concepts (copy in the City of Los Angeles EIR references: https://planning.lacity.gov/eir/8150Sunset/References/4.G.%20Noise/N.05_%20FTA%20Noise%20and%20Vibration%20Impact%20Assessment%20Chapter%207_1995.pdf)

global_low.quote: a hypothetical background spectrum that is unlikely to be duplicated at any single location on Earth

global_high.quote: a spectrum of average high background noise power in the network

band_limit_hz.quote: Line parameters for constructing the NLNM curve given the period (P)
band_limit_hz.note: the tables start at P = 0.10 s: the models say nothing above 10 Hz

microseism_vertical_0.1_0.3_hz.note: median, 10th-90th percentile; Kottamya, 67 km east of Giza; the band is regional

vertical_1_3_hz.note: a quiet hill: a lower bound for Giza above 1 Hz

giza_ground_hz.quote: the average predominant frequency on the surrounding ground is about 0.60 Hz

khufu_pyramid_hz.quote: fundamental frequency between 2.0 and 2.6, with an average of ~ 2.3

cultural.reference: RMS over 1 s, VdB re 1e-6 in/s (2.54e-8 m/s), 50 ft (15.2 m) from the source, above 8 Hz; levels read from Figure 7-3 unless quoted

urban_background.note: Figure 7-3; 'Background vibration is usually well below the threshold of human perception'

bus_or_truck_over_bump.quote: Buses and trucks rarely create vibration that exceeds 70 VdB unless there are bumps in the road

human_perception.quote: threshold of perception for humans which is around 65 VdB

band_hz.quote: At frequencies greater than 8 Hz, which for all practical purposes is the frequency range of interest to ground-borne vibration
